## 1. LOCATION OVERVIEW

Southampton’s garden conditions change sharply between its wooded, higher northern suburbs, its stream valleys and its low tidal edges. Southampton City Council’s drainage guidance places London Clay mainly in the north, Wittering Formation mainly in the south, river-terrace deposits on higher ground and tidal-flat deposits beside the Test and Itchen. It also says the city’s urban soils are largely unsurveyed: some investigated sites have slowly permeable, seasonally waterlogged ground, but no neighbourhood-wide soil or acidity classification follows from the bedrock map.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf] Northern ground commonly reaches 50–60 metres above Ordnance Datum; reclaimed coastal land can be as low as 0.5–1 metre. Steeper ground is generally northern and eastern, while land near the tidal rivers is flatter.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf]

The distinction matters for landscaping. The council identifies tidal flooding as Southampton’s principal flood source, naming St Denys, Bitterne Manor’s frontage and the lower Itchen among affected places; Holly Brook, Tanners Brook and Monks Brook create separate inland risks.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] In Bassett, documented quarter-acre plots and substantial trees contrast with the tighter terraces of Hollybrook and the Flowers Estate.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf] Highfield’s garden-suburb conservation areas add unusually specific controls over visible gardens, paths, boundaries and trees.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/4ian33xb/portswood_residents_garden_conservation_area_af.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ni3f52xv/otra-character-appraisal-management-plan_tcm63-363345.pdf] Old Woolston has another pattern: generous villa gardens survive within a denser, slightly hilly eastern suburb.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/yyncgowi/woolston_conservation_area_appraisal_january_2010_tcm63-363376.pdf]

Southampton City Council is the planning and highways authority for the areas profiled here.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/travel-transport/apply-pay/licences/dropped-kerbs/policy-terms-and-conditions/] Water is a separate constraint: Southern Water’s Hampshire and Isle of Wight hosepipe restrictions, introduced on **10 July 2026**, were reported still in force in early October 2026 **(dated: October 2026)**.[https://www.ccw.org.uk/news/hosepipe-restrictions-why-are-they-happening-and-are-you-affected/][https://www.preparedbritain.co.uk/trackers/hosepipe-bans]

## 2. NEIGHBOURHOOD PROFILES

### [SOU-N01] St Denys | neighbourhood
Profile: **Priory Road’s riverside gardens are explicitly identified in Southampton’s flood assessment as exposed to tidal overtopping.** The assessment says flooding there can remain in gardens but can also reach buildings; it describes the lower Itchen as tidal through the city.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] This makes garden levels, surface-water routes and the position of patios or decking materially different from work on Southampton’s higher ground (inferred). The assessment does not establish a uniform soil, garden size or housing type for all of St Denys; this profile concerns its documented riverside plots.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]  
Linked issues: SOU-I02, SOU-I03

### [SOU-N02] Bitterne Manor | neighbourhood
Profile: **The Bitterne Manor frontage is among the council’s named locations at particular tidal-flood risk.** The designation concerns its waterside edge, not every garden inland.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf] Southampton’s drainage guidance also identifies tidal-flat deposits beside the Itchen and potentially high groundwater close to the city’s tidal rivers.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf] On frontage plots, these conditions bear on drainage outlets, below-ground work and the siting of hard surfaces (inferred). No reliable area-wide measurement of garden dimensions, acidity or salt exposure was found.  
Linked issues: SOU-I01, SOU-I02

### [SOU-N03] Swaythling | neighbourhood
Profile: **Brookside Way, Monks Way and Wessex Lane are named together in the city’s assessment of out-of-bank flooding from Monks Brook.** The assessment distinguishes that inland river risk from flooding on the tidal Itchen frontage.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] Low ground beside the brook consequently presents a different drainage setting from Swaythling’s higher residential plots (inferred). The evidence identifies streets and a watercourse, but not a single housing era, garden size or soil-acidity value for Swaythling as a whole.  
Linked issues: SOU-I03, SOU-I04

### [SOU-N04] Hollybrook and Dale Valley | neighbourhood
Profile: **Holly Brook runs through Dale Valley Close, taking runoff from the City Golf Course and woods beside the Outdoor Sports Centre.** The Bassett Neighbourhood Plan describes Hollybrook’s medium and small terraced, semi-detached and detached family houses, while Dale Valley Close and Dale Valley Gardens are mainly bungalows.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf] The flood assessment identifies Dale Road, Dale Valley Road and Dale Valley Close as locations affected by brook overflow or constrained culverts; it also identifies the Holly Brook corridor as having high groundwater-flood susceptibility.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] These are stronger grounds for drainage-led work than an unverified claim that every plot has clay soil.  
Linked issues: SOU-I01, SOU-I03, SOU-I04

### [SOU-N05] Shirley | neighbourhood
Profile: **The council’s drainage guidance records previous groundwater-flood incidents in Shirley.** Its strategic flood assessment also names streets on the Tanners Brook system and says parts of Shirley rely on pumping stations to assist surface-water discharge.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] These are distinct mechanisms: water can emerge or persist below ground, arrive along a brook corridor, or accumulate as runoff (inferred). The records do not establish that all Shirley gardens flood, nor do they give a consistent local plot size or soil-acidity class.  
Linked issues: SOU-I01, SOU-I03

### [SOU-N06] Millbrook | neighbourhood
Profile: **Millbrook is identified as exposed to combined River Test tidal and fluvial flooding.** The city’s flood assessment adds that many surface-water outlets in its catchment sit below high-tide level and can be tide-locked; parts of Millbrook depend on pumping stations for surface-water discharge.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] That combination is relevant to drainage and hard landscaping on lower plots, particularly where a paved surface sends additional runoff toward an outlet (inferred). The documented risk should not be read as a description of every Millbrook garden.  
Linked issues: SOU-I01, SOU-I02, SOU-I03

### [SOU-N07] Bassett Heath | neighbourhood
Profile: **Bassett Heath Avenue and nearby Bassett Dale, Saxholm Way, Saxholm Dale and Pinehurst Road contain large detached family houses, many on approximately quarter-acre plots.** The neighbourhood plan identifies long, narrow plots in several of these roads and describes Bassett’s undulating, tree-rich setting.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf] Long plots and mature planting give landscape layout and tree-root protection a more substantial role than in compact terraced streets (inferred). The council’s city-wide geology places London Clay principally in northern Southampton, but the available evidence does not prove the soil beneath each Bassett Heath garden is clay.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf]  
Linked issues: SOU-I01, SOU-I04, SOU-I05, SOU-I06

### [SOU-N08] Ridgemount Area | neighbourhood
Profile: **Ardnave Crescent, Greenbank Crescent and Ridgemount Avenue are specifically described as large detached houses with large gardens.** The Bassett Neighbourhood Plan puts existing density in the Ridgemount Area at approximately eight to fifteen dwellings per hectare.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf] The spacious plots create room for distinct lawn, planting and hard-landscape areas, while making established trees and the relationship between works and neighbouring plots significant (inferred). The plan provides no reliable garden-by-garden access width, soil pH or mapped species inventory.  
Linked issues: SOU-I04, SOU-I05, SOU-I06

### [SOU-N09] Flowers Estate | estate
Profile: **The Flowers Estate is described as former council family housing made up largely of semi-detached and terraced properties; the neighbourhood plan also identifies its relatively high density.** It records that many properties subsequently became houses in multiple occupation.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf] This is a different plot setting from Bassett’s quarter-acre roads: work on garden surfaces, boundaries and maintenance takes place within a tighter housing pattern (inferred). The plan does not quantify the estate’s individual back gardens or establish that all have the same access arrangement.  
Linked issues: SOU-I01, SOU-I06, SOU-I07

### [SOU-N10] Ethelburt Avenue and Bassett Green Estate | estate
Profile: **Two-storey pairs and short terraces are grouped around small greens in this designated conservation area.** It covers Ethelburt Avenue and parts of Leaside Way, Bassett Green Road, Stoneham Lane and Field Close; landscaped front gardens, some with clipped privet hedges, are characteristic.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/bhlodkjj/ethelburt-avenue-conservation-area-appraisal-management-plan-approved_af.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/planning/heritage/conservation-areas/ethelburt-avenue/] The appraisal identifies Scots pine on estate greens, cherries along Ethelburt Avenue and low retaining walls where some gardens stand above the footway. It also documents controls on additional hard surfaces, front enclosures and tree works.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/bhlodkjj/ethelburt-avenue-conservation-area-appraisal-management-plan-approved_af.pdf]  
Linked issues: SOU-I04, SOU-I05, SOU-I06, SOU-I07

### [SOU-N11] Portswood Residents’ Gardens | estate
Profile: **This estate’s houses were built mainly between 1908 and 1930 in generous, leafy plots arranged around two communal gardens.** Its original layout specified frontages of 75 feet on Brookvale Road and 60 feet elsewhere, with a building line at least 30 feet behind the plot front.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/4ian33xb/portswood_residents_garden_conservation_area_af.pdf] Mature private gardens, a meadow, allotments, a stream and numerous trees are identified as part of its character. Visible hardstanding, paths and boundary alterations face conservation-area and Article 4 controls, making the front-garden layout especially consequential for paving and fencing work.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/4ian33xb/portswood_residents_garden_conservation_area_af.pdf]  
Linked issues: SOU-I05, SOU-I06, SOU-I07

### [SOU-N12] Oakmount Triangle | neighbourhood
Profile: **Oakmount Triangle’s appraisal calculates a mean house-plot area of 0.063 hectares and describes small front gardens behind low red-brown brick walls.** The area covers Blenheim Avenue, Leigh Road, Oakmount Avenue and Westbourne Crescent, with specified adjoining properties.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ni3f52xv/otra-character-appraisal-management-plan_tcm63-363345.pdf] Gaps between houses reveal back gardens, while ornamental trees and shrubs contribute strongly to the street scene. The appraisal records an Article 4 direction covering visible hard surfaces, paths and boundaries, and resists replacing planted front gardens with vehicle hardstanding.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ni3f52xv/otra-character-appraisal-management-plan_tcm63-363345.pdf]  
Linked issues: SOU-I05, SOU-I06, SOU-I07

### [SOU-N13] Uplands Estate, Highfield | estate
Profile: **Uplands Estate combines short terraces and semi-detached houses with communal landscaped areas, grass verges, open-plan front gardens and clipped hedges.** Its estate design guidance describes roads that dip and rise with the land and houses positioned around retained mature trees and shared open space.[http://www.ueha.co.uk/uploads/2/5/6/4/25647797/ueha__conservation_guidelines__aug_2020.pdf] Individual gardens and shared or undivided front areas therefore have different boundary conditions within the same estate. A conservation designation and Article 4 direction add controls to alterations; the detailed estate guide was available from the homeowners’ association after the council-hosted copy failed to open.[http://www.ueha.co.uk/uploads/2/5/6/4/25647797/ueha__conservation_guidelines__aug_2020.pdf]  
Linked issues: SOU-I04, SOU-I05, SOU-I06, SOU-I07

### [SOU-N14] Old Woolston | neighbourhood
Profile: **Old Woolston’s conservation-area appraisal records large late-Victorian villas with generous private gardens on parts of Oak and Obelisk roads, alongside later subdivision into smaller plots.** It names lime, acacia, oak, beech and sycamore as prominent trees in the Oak Road area.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/yyncgowi/woolston_conservation_area_appraisal_january_2010_tcm63-363376.pdf] The suburb is slightly hilly; the Portsmouth Road conservation-area plots rise fairly steeply away from the Itchen and include mature trees and substantial front gardens.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/yyncgowi/woolston_conservation_area_appraisal_january_2010_tcm63-363376.pdf] That combination links tree work, level changes, retaining features and sympathetic boundary treatment to particular streets, rather than to Woolston uniformly (inferred).  
Linked issues: SOU-I04, SOU-I05, SOU-I06

### [SOU-N15] St Anne’s Road, Woolston | neighbourhood
Profile: **The St Anne’s Road Conservation Area comprises a small group of large, predominantly mid- to late-Victorian detached properties on a wide, tree-lined road.** The Woolston appraisal records mature trees and vegetation along many boundaries; it also notes that several villa front gardens had been partly replaced by hardstanding when surveyed.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/yyncgowi/woolston_conservation_area_appraisal_january_2010_tcm63-363376.pdf] This makes preservation of remaining planted frontage and treatment of walls, gates and parking surfaces a specifically documented local issue. The appraisal recommended possible additional Article 4 controls; a recommendation is not evidence that those directions took effect.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/yyncgowi/woolston_conservation_area_appraisal_january_2010_tcm63-363376.pdf]  
Linked issues: SOU-I05, SOU-I06

### [SOU-N16] Townhill Park | estate
Profile: **Townhill Park is one of the areas the city’s flood assessment identified as susceptible to groundwater flooding after the exceptionally wet winter of 2013–14.** The council also documents estate regeneration and a new central green space, Townhill Green **(dated: September 2025)**.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/housing/council-housing-tenants-and-leaseholders/repairs-maintenance-and-improvements/improvements-we-are-making/estate-regeneration/townhill-park-regeneration/] The groundwater record is relevant to low spots and below-ground landscape components, but it does not establish a uniform water table across the estate (inferred). Available official material does not give dependable estate-wide garden measurements or an acidity classification.  
Linked issues: SOU-I01, SOU-I06

### [SOU-N17] Lordswood | neighbourhood
Profile: **The Bassett Neighbourhood Plan describes Lordswood as mainly detached family housing, with larger detached homes on Lordswood Road, Lordswood Close and Lordswood Gardens.** It identifies Lordswood Close as an unmade private close.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf] The wider Southampton flood assessment places parts of Lordswood within the Holly Brook and Tanners Brook flood outline, rather than treating all its higher residential plots as floodplain.[https://www.push.gov.uk/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/Southampton.pdf] Work involving long private plots or an unmade access road has a different physical setting from a paved urban terrace (inferred); measured local garden sizes remain unavailable.  
Linked issues: SOU-I03, SOU-I04, SOU-I06

### [SOU-N18] Freemantle | neighbourhood
Profile: **Parts of Freemantle rely on pumping stations to assist surface-water discharge, according to Southampton’s strategic flood assessment.** That is a catchment-level drainage characteristic, not evidence that every garden floods.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] The same assessment identifies urban development and relatively impermeable geology as contributors to city-wide runoff, particularly where overland routes are obstructed.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] These records support attention to the direction in which new paving sheds water (inferred). Reliable official measurements of Freemantle plot dimensions, access widths and soil acidity were not found.  
Linked issues: SOU-I01, SOU-I03, SOU-I06

### [SOU-N19] Woodmill | neighbourhood
Profile: **The city’s flood assessment locates tide-locking where the freshwater Itchen meets its tidal estuary at Woodmill.** It separately identifies Oliver Road back gardens as subject to tidal overtopping in a modelled present-day event, with Woodmill Lane also affected.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] The combination makes low riverside garden levels and discharge routes especially significant for landscaping and decking (inferred). The evidence is precise about those locations; it does not support extending the same flood depth to Woodmill’s other properties.  
Linked issues: SOU-I02, SOU-I03, SOU-I04

### [SOU-N20] Northam | neighbourhood
Profile: **Northam is repeatedly named among Southampton’s lower Itchen tidal-risk areas.** The strategic flood assessment describes low ground north of the Itchen Bridge at risk in its modelled tidal event and identifies frontage locations around Northam Bridge.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] Much of the cited frontage is industrial or commercial rather than conventional private garden land; the distinction limits the direct residential landscaping inference.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] Where outdoor works do occur on low frontage plots, tidal levels and existing drainage arrangements are more relevant than a city-wide assumption about soil type (inferred).  
Linked issues: SOU-I01, SOU-I02, SOU-I03

## 3. LOCAL ISSUES

### [SOU-I01] Mixed geology and locally slow-draining ground
Detail: Southampton cannot accurately be described as having one garden soil. Council SuDS guidance maps London Clay predominantly in the north, Wittering Formation predominantly in the south, river-terrace material on higher ground and tidal-flat deposits by the Test and Itchen. It explicitly says urban soils are largely unsurveyed, although investigated sites include slowly permeable, seasonally waterlogged ground, particularly towards the coast and reclaimed land.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf] Thus Bassett Heath [SOU-N07] and Hollybrook [SOU-N04] lie in the broad northern geological zone, while Bitterne Manor’s frontage [SOU-N02], Millbrook [SOU-N06] and Northam [SOU-N20] illustrate lower waterside settings; assigning a soil type to an individual garden from that zone is **(inferred)**.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf]

The practical distinction is between a surface that lets water through and ground that can receive it. The council says impermeable soils and high groundwater can make infiltration drainage unsuitable; it discusses shallow, lined or above-ground attenuation where those constraints occur.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf] It specifies that a soakaway base should be at least one metre above the maximum likely groundwater level and five metres from foundations and subsurface structures.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf] For lawns, paths, patios and driveway landscaping, persistent wet patches and the destination of runoff are therefore separate physical questions (inferred). Shirley’s recorded groundwater incidents [SOU-N05] and Townhill Park’s identified susceptibility [SOU-N16] strengthen the local relevance without proving every plot there is waterlogged.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]  
Scope: Local  
Category tags: Gardener; Landscape Gardener; Landscape Designer; Lawn care service; Paving contractor  
Service tags: Lawn care; Lawn landscaping; Grass seeding; Sod installation; Garden drainage; Drainage solutions; Garden levelling; Grading and resloping; Excavation & grading; Driveway or path paving; Patio paving  
Angles:
- **Cause:** A permeable paving surface does not, by itself, establish that the soil beneath can absorb its stored water (inferred).
- **Timing:** The council identifies seasonal waterlogging and groundwater levels that vary through the year.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf]
- **Property type:** Reclaimed and riverside land has a different documented groundwater setting from higher river-terrace ground.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf]
Condition question: Why does water remain beneath my lawn or paving after rain?  
Answer material: Southampton’s mapped geology varies, and the council reports slowly permeable soils at some investigated sites rather than across every neighbourhood.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf] Groundwater can also be high close to the rivers and watercourses, so persistent wetness can have more than one local cause.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf]

### [SOU-I02] Tidal water reaching low riverside gardens
Detail: The Test and Itchen form approximately 35 kilometres of tidal frontage within Southampton’s flood assessment, which identifies the sea as the city’s primary flood source.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] The council names St Denys [SOU-N01], Bitterne Manor’s frontage [SOU-N02], Northam [SOU-N20] and other lower Itchen locations as particularly exposed.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf] Its assessment is unusually specific about gardens: properties and gardens on Priory Road in St Denys, and back gardens on Oliver Road near Woodmill [SOU-N19], appear in its present-day tidal-overtopping account. Modelled depths for the cited Oliver Road back gardens are approximately 0.4–0.9 metres in the stated event, not a prediction for every nearby plot.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]

High water can affect more than a garden’s visible edge. Council drainage guidance explains that a downstream river or tide can prevent an outlet discharging, while high groundwater is possible near the Test and Itchen, especially on reclaimed land.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf] Millbrook [SOU-N06] adds a Test-side example of combined tidal and river exposure.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] For landscape construction, low patio and deck levels, buried drainage components and raised ground can consequently change where water collects or flows (inferred). This issue belongs to specified low frontages, not Bassett’s elevated plots.  
Scope: Local  
Category tags: Landscape Gardener; Landscape Designer; Paving contractor; Deck builder  
Service tags: Garden drainage; Drainage solutions; Grading and resloping; Retaining walls; Retaining wall design; Patio design; Patio paving; Deck design; Deck installation; Garden landscaping  
Angles:
- **Cause:** Tidal overtopping and tide-locked drainage outlets are distinct ways water can reach or remain on a low plot.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]
- **Property type:** Priory Road gardens and Oliver Road back gardens are named residential examples; much Northam frontage is commercial.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]
- **Consequence:** Raising one garden level can redirect floodwater or create ponding elsewhere, as the council’s assessment explains.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]
Condition question: Why has water reached the back garden when there has been little local rain?  
Answer material: Southampton’s rivers are tidal through much of the city, and the flood assessment expressly identifies overtopping affecting particular St Denys and Woodmill gardens.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] A high tide can also impede an existing surface-water outlet.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf]

### [SOU-I03] Brook corridors, culverts and tide-locked surface drainage
Detail: Southampton’s inland watercourses create a second, more street-specific water problem. The strategic flood assessment identifies Holly Brook overflow or constrained culverts around Dale Road, Dale Valley Road and Dale Valley Close [SOU-N04]; Tanners Brook locations include streets in the Shirley and western catchment [SOU-N05], while Brookside Way, Monks Way and Wessex Lane [SOU-N03] are identified on Monks Brook.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] The assessment also places parts of Lordswood [SOU-N17] within the Holly Brook and Tanners Brook flood outline.[https://www.push.gov.uk/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/Southampton.pdf] These findings concern watercourse corridors and flow paths, not a blanket designation of whole neighbourhoods.

Urban runoff adds another mechanism. The council says surface-water flooding can occur across the built-up city and that valleys, hollows, hill bottoms and blocked overland routes can concentrate it.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] In the Millbrook [SOU-N06] and Portswood catchments, some outlets lie below high-tide level; Freemantle [SOU-N18], Millbrook and Shirley also contain areas assisted by pumping stations.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] The council’s drainage guidance describes swales along development boundaries as one way to intercept incoming runoff and identifies storage as relevant when a high river or tide prevents discharge.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf] In garden terms, replacing absorbent ground with paving or changing a slope can alter a pre-existing route for rainwater (inferred).  
Scope: Local

- **Cause:** Holly Brook, Tanners Brook and Monks Brook have separately documented residential flood locations.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]
- **Timing:** Tide-locking is most significant when high tide and intense rainfall coincide.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]
- **Consequence:** A blocked or altered overland route can concentrate runoff in a lower garden (inferred).
Condition question: Why does rainwater run through my garden rather than drain where it falls?  
Answer material: Southampton’s assessment identifies important overland routes through its urban valleys and hollows, as well as particular brook and culvert flood locations.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] It also identifies catchments where high tide can stop surface-water outlets discharging normally.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]

### [SOU-I04] Undulating plots and faster runoff on slopes
Detail: Southampton’s council drainage guidance locates steeper land mainly in the north and east and describes the city as generally descending towards the Test, Itchen and coast.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf] That broad pattern becomes concrete in Bassett: the neighbourhood plan calls its terrain undulating, describes a valley associated with the City Golf Course and Outdoor Sports Centre, and locates Holly Brook runoff from those grounds through Dale Valley [SOU-N04].[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf] Uplands Estate [SOU-N13] was arranged around roads that rise and dip, while Old Woolston’s Portsmouth Road plots [SOU-N14] rise fairly steeply from the river.[http://www.ueha.co.uk/uploads/2/5/6/4/25647797/ueha__conservation_guidelines__aug_2020.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/yyncgowi/woolston_conservation_area_appraisal_january_2010_tcm63-363376.pdf] Bassett Heath [SOU-N07], Ridgemount [SOU-N08], Lordswood [SOU-N17] and Woodmill [SOU-N19] each need their actual plot position distinguished from that wider topographic setting (inferred).

For construction, the council says steep slopes increase runoff velocity and that storing or infiltrating water can affect slope stability. Its guidance describes staged, terraced storage as a response to steep sites, in contrast to shallow surface conveyance on flatter ground.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf] A patio, outdoor step, deck support or retaining feature therefore does more than create a level surface: it can interrupt or redirect water moving downslope (inferred). The council also cautions that raising ground levels can deflect flood flows or increase ponding on another property.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]  
Scope: Local  
Category tags: Landscape Gardener; Landscape Designer; Paving contractor; Deck builder  
Service tags: Garden levelling; Grading and resloping; Retaining walls; Retaining wall design; Outdoor step construction; Excavation & grading; Path landscaping; Patio design; Patio paving; Deck design; Deck installation  
Angles:
- **Cause:** Southampton’s higher northern and eastern ground includes steeper slopes than its low tidal margins.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf]
- **Property type:** Bassett’s larger, sometimes long plots differ from the terraced housing beside Holly Brook.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf]
- **Consequence:** A change of level can change both runoff speed and its destination (inferred).
Condition question: Why does water wash across the path and collect at the bottom of the garden?  
Answer material: The council identifies greater runoff velocity on steep slopes and a concentration of surface-water risk in hollows and hill bottoms.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] Its guidance treats staged storage and slope stability as connected design considerations.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf]

### [SOU-I05] Mature trees within working garden plots
Detail: Bassett’s neighbourhood plan identifies substantial established redwood, sweet chestnut, cedar, oak and western hemlock and treats trees as central to the area’s character.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf] The contrast between Bassett Heath’s larger plots [SOU-N07] and the smaller Flowers Estate [SOU-N09] means there is no single Southampton pattern of tree cover (inferred). Elsewhere, Portswood Residents’ Gardens [SOU-N11] has documented oaks, limes, cherries, whitebeams and many other trees in communal and private spaces; Oakmount Triangle [SOU-N12] identifies mature ornamental trees and shrubs; Old Woolston’s Oak Road [SOU-N14] records lime, acacia, oak, beech and sycamore.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/4ian33xb/portswood_residents_garden_conservation_area_af.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ni3f52xv/otra-character-appraisal-management-plan_tcm63-363345.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/yyncgowi/woolston_conservation_area_appraisal_january_2010_tcm63-363376.pdf]

The trees affect both maintenance and construction. Southampton has more than 700 Tree Preservation Orders, and the council’s map separately shows TPO and conservation-area layers; protected trees cannot simply be pruned or removed as an incidental part of garden work.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/environment/trees-grass-hedges-and-leaves/protected/][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/environment/trees-grass-hedges-and-leaves/protected/tpo-map/] The council also confirms ash dieback at a small number of its sites across the city, **without naming an affected neighbourhood**.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/environment/trees-grass-hedges-and-leaves/reporting-issues-with-trees-or-vegetation/nuisance-trees/] That does not justify diagnosing an individual garden ash (inferred). Around mature trees, paving, excavation, stump work, fencing and deck supports intersect with established planting and sometimes statutory protection (inferred).  
Scope: Local  
Category tags: Gardener; Landscape Gardener; Landscape Designer; Tree service; Paving contractor; Deck builder  
Service tags: Tree trimming and pruning; Tree removal; Tree planting; Tree stump grinding; Tree stump removal; Landscape design; Garden design; Landscape installations; Driveway or path paving; Deck design; Deck installation  
Angles:
- **Property type:** Bassett’s large detached plots and Highfield’s planted communal gardens offer different tree-work settings.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/4ian33xb/portswood_residents_garden_conservation_area_af.pdf]
- **Cause:** Southampton’s protected-tree system covers individual trees, groups and woodland.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/environment/trees-grass-hedges-and-leaves/protected/]
- **Consequence:** Removing or damaging a mature tree can alter an established conservation-area streetscape.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/4ian33xb/portswood_residents_garden_conservation_area_af.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ni3f52xv/otra-character-appraisal-management-plan_tcm63-363345.pdf]
Condition question: Why does the tree over my garden affect the planned path or deck?  
Answer material: Established trees form part of several specifically appraised Southampton landscapes, and the council protects some through TPOs or conservation-area controls.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/environment/trees-grass-hedges-and-leaves/protected/tpo-map/] Those controls apply to tree work independently of whether a new garden surface is proposed.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/environment/trees-grass-hedges-and-leaves/protected/]

### [SOU-I06] Contrasting plot sizes, frontages and access
Detail: Southampton contains unusually well-documented differences in residential plot form. Bassett’s neighbourhood plan identifies quarter-acre plots around Bassett Heath [SOU-N07], large gardens in Ridgemount [SOU-N08], and terraced or semi-detached family housing in Hollybrook [SOU-N04] and the Flowers Estate [SOU-N09].[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf] Portswood Residents’ Gardens [SOU-N11] was laid out with generous specified frontages and setbacks, whereas Oakmount Triangle [SOU-N12] combines small front gardens and visible gaps between individual houses.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/4ian33xb/portswood_residents_garden_conservation_area_af.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ni3f52xv/otra-character-appraisal-management-plan_tcm63-363345.pdf] Uplands [SOU-N13] adds shared landscaped space and some undivided front gardens; Ethelburt Avenue [SOU-N10] has greens and front lawns whose ownership and upkeep do not always follow an ordinary private-garden pattern.[http://www.ueha.co.uk/uploads/2/5/6/4/25647797/ueha__conservation_guidelines__aug_2020.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/bhlodkjj/ethelburt-avenue-conservation-area-appraisal-management-plan-approved_af.pdf]

This affects what constitutes a garden boundary, the room available for lawn or drainage features, and the route by which materials reach a rear plot (inferred). It also matters at the street edge. Southampton’s crossover policy requires a sufficiently deep parking space, sets a standard crossing width of 4.6 metres, allows only one crossing into a property and prohibits one within one metre of a tree trunk, with greater separation possible for a larger tree.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/travel-transport/apply-pay/licences/dropped-kerbs/policy-terms-and-conditions/] A small front garden is therefore not interchangeable with an existing driveway or a Bassett-size plot (inferred).  
Scope: Local  
Category tags: Gardener; Landscape Gardener; Landscape Designer; Lawn care service; Tree service; Paving contractor; Deck builder  
Service tags: Lawn mowing and maintenance; Lawn care; Garden work; Fencing installation; Garden design; Custom landscape design; Landscape management; Driveway landscaping; Driveway installation; Driveway replacement; Patio paving; Deck design; Deck installation  
Angles:
- **Property type:** Quarter-acre Bassett plots and tighter former council terraces create materially different usable garden areas.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf]
- **Access:** Some estate front lawns and communal greens are not ordinary privately owned extensions of a driveway.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/bhlodkjj/ethelburt-avenue-conservation-area-appraisal-management-plan-approved_af.pdf][http://www.ueha.co.uk/uploads/2/5/6/4/25647797/ueha__conservation_guidelines__aug_2020.pdf]
- **Consequence:** The city’s crossing dimensions and tree separation constrain a new vehicle entrance even where space for paving appears available.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/travel-transport/apply-pay/licences/dropped-kerbs/policy-terms-and-conditions/]
Condition question: Why is there less room for a driveway and planted front garden than the frontage suggests?  
Answer material: Plot layouts vary markedly by Southampton estate, and shared greens or characteristic open frontages occur in several conservation areas.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/bhlodkjj/ethelburt-avenue-conservation-area-appraisal-management-plan-approved_af.pdf][http://www.ueha.co.uk/uploads/2/5/6/4/25647797/ueha__conservation_guidelines__aug_2020.pdf] The council’s vehicle-crossing policy separately limits parking-space dimensions, crossing width and proximity to a tree.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/travel-transport/apply-pay/licences/dropped-kerbs/policy-terms-and-conditions/]

### [SOU-I07] Water restrictions alongside lawns and new planting
Detail: Southern Water draws attention to the Test and Itchen chalk streams as important sources of Hampshire and Isle of Wight drinking water.[https://www.southernwater.co.uk/latest-news/end-of-hosepipe-ban-for-hampshire-and-isle-of-wight/] A Temporary Use Ban affecting its customers in those supply areas began on **10 July 2026**; consumer-water information in September and an early-October tracker continued to list the restriction **(dated: October 2026)**.[https://www.itv.com/news/meridian/2026-07-10/hosepipe-ban-comes-into-force-as-third-heatwave-hits][https://www.ccw.org.uk/news/hosepipe-restrictions-why-are-they-happening-and-are-you-affected/][https://www.preparedbritain.co.uk/trackers/hosepipe-bans] The restriction makes water availability a distinctive current condition for Southampton lawns, planted borders, hedges and new turf, whether the plot is a large Bassett garden [SOU-N07], a planted Highfield estate frontage [SOU-N11–N13] or a tighter Flowers Estate garden [SOU-N09] (inferred).

The reported ban prohibits using a hosepipe for ordinary garden watering; watering cans and buckets remain permitted, subject to the published exemptions.[https://www.itv.com/news/meridian/2026-07-10/hosepipe-ban-comes-into-force-as-third-heatwave-hits][https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c17yv9710d9o] Southern Water lists a qualified exemption for certain trees, saplings and hedging planted during the preceding three years where watering cannot reasonably be done by can, and specifies conditions for drip or trickle systems.[https://www.southernwater.co.uk/help-and-support/hosepipe-ban-exemptions/] Those qualifications should not be flattened into a claim that all new planting may be hose-watered (inferred). This issue differs from the city’s winter waterlogging: a garden may have poor infiltration during wet weather and still face mains-water restrictions during drought (inferred).  
Scope: Regional  
Category tags: Gardener; Landscape Gardener; Landscape Designer; Lawn care service; Tree service  
Service tags: Lawn care; Lawn landscaping; Turf management; Grass seeding; Sod installation; Garden landscaping; Green landscaping; Mulching; Tree planting; Landscape management  
Angles:
- **Timing:** The cited restriction began in July 2026 and remained reported in force in early October **(dated: October 2026)**.[https://www.itv.com/news/meridian/2026-07-10/hosepipe-ban-comes-into-force-as-third-heatwave-hits][https://www.preparedbritain.co.uk/trackers/hosepipe-bans]
- **Water source:** Southern Water connects its restrictions with pressure on the Test and Itchen.[https://www.southernwater.co.uk/latest-news/end-of-hosepipe-ban-for-hampshire-and-isle-of-wight/]
- **Property type:** A large lawn and a small estate front garden face the same supply-area restriction but have different planted areas (inferred).
Condition question: Why is watering the new lawn with a hose restricted?  
Answer material: Southern Water’s Hampshire and Isle of Wight Temporary Use Ban covers ordinary hosepipe garden watering **(dated: October 2026)**.[https://www.itv.com/news/meridian/2026-07-10/hosepipe-ban-comes-into-force-as-third-heatwave-hits][https://www.preparedbritain.co.uk/trackers/hosepipe-bans] Its published exemptions distinguish some recently planted trees and hedging from general lawn watering.[https://www.southernwater.co.uk/help-and-support/hosepipe-ban-exemptions/]

## 5. RULES & COUNCIL

### [SOU-R01] Southampton Tree Preservation Orders and conservation-area tree controls
Detail: Southampton City Council says a TPO can protect an individual tree, group or woodland against unauthorised pruning, damage or removal. Its online map displays TPOs in blue and conservation-area protection in red and provides TPO documents; the map’s layers are indicative. In conservation areas, the council identifies the protected-tree threshold as a trunk diameter greater than 75 millimetres at 1.5 metres above ground; its Ethelburt appraisal specifies six weeks’ notice for applicable work.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/environment/trees-grass-hedges-and-leaves/protected/][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/environment/trees-grass-hedges-and-leaves/protected/tpo-map/][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/bhlodkjj/ethelburt-avenue-conservation-area-appraisal-management-plan-approved_af.pdf] These controls affect tree services and excavation near protected planting.  
Applies to: SOU-N07, SOU-N08, SOU-N10, SOU-N11, SOU-N12, SOU-N13, SOU-N14, SOU-N15, and other protected-tree plots across the whole area

### [SOU-R02] Portswood Residents’ Gardens Conservation Area Appraisal, Management Plan and Article 4(2) Direction
Detail: Policy PRG 6 retains front gardens and says enlarging vehicle hardstandings or drives requires permission that will not normally be granted; it presumes against a second vehicle access. It describes new tarmac and concrete surfacing as inappropriate except when repairing an existing such surface. PRG 7 controls alteration or demolition of front and boundary walls and fences. The Article 4 schedule additionally covers hard surfaces, including paths, and gates, fences or walls where the development fronts a highway, waterway or open space; the schedule specifies the affected properties.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/4ian33xb/portswood_residents_garden_conservation_area_af.pdf]  
Applies to: SOU-N11

### [SOU-R03] Oakmount Triangle Conservation Area Appraisal, Management Plan and Article 4(2) Direction
Detail: Oakmount’s Article 4 schedule removes specified permitted-development rights for hard surfaces and paths, and for erection, alteration or demolition of gates, fences and walls fronting a highway, waterway or open space. The appraisal resists replacing planted front gardens with vehicle hardstanding and generally resists demolition of characteristic boundary walls unless appropriately rebuilt. Its conservation-area controls also apply to qualifying trees.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ni3f52xv/otra-character-appraisal-management-plan_tcm63-363345.pdf] The requirements are specific to the direction’s property schedule, not all neighbouring Highfield streets.  
Applies to: SOU-N12

### [SOU-R04] Ethelburt Avenue Conservation Area Appraisal, Management Plan and Article 4 Direction
Detail: The management plan discourages additional hard surfaces that remove planting and says enclosing front gardens with new walls or fences requires permission and will be resisted. Its Article 4 material identifies visible paths, hardstandings and boundary enclosures among controlled works; the document records property exclusions in Field Close and Stoneham Lane. It also specifies six weeks’ notice for qualifying conservation-area tree work and treats estate greens as open ornamental spaces rather than building plots.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/bhlodkjj/ethelburt-avenue-conservation-area-appraisal-management-plan-approved_af.pdf]  
Applies to: SOU-N10

### [SOU-R05] Uplands Estate (Highfield) Conservation Area and Article 4 Direction
Detail: Uplands has an Article 4 direction restricting otherwise permitted works to specified elevations, roofs, pools and garden buildings or enclosures.[http://www.ueha.co.uk/uploads/2/5/6/4/25647797/ueha__conservation_guidelines__aug_2020.pdf] The estate design guide describes open front gardens, low clipped hedges and characteristic paths; it says front gardens should not become parking spaces and distinguishes freeholder consent from planning permission. This guide was read on the homeowners’ association’s site after the council-hosted document did not open; its account of estate-specific permissions should therefore not be mistaken for the text of a council planning decision.[http://www.ueha.co.uk/uploads/2/5/6/4/25647797/ueha__conservation_guidelines__aug_2020.pdf]  
Applies to: SOU-N13

### [SOU-R06] Southampton City Council dropped-kerb policy and front-driveway drainage
Detail: The council says an impermeable driveway covering more than five square metres requires planning permission if runoff is not controlled; permeable surfacing or discharge into a lawn or border is treated differently. Water must not run onto the highway. Its crossing policy sets minimum on-plot parking dimensions, a normal 4.6-metre crossing width, one crossing per property and at least one metre between a crossing and a tree trunk. A classified-road crossing additionally requires planning permission.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/travel-transport/apply-pay/licences/dropped-kerbs/policy-terms-and-conditions/][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/travel-transport/apply-pay/licences/dropped-kerbs/]  
Applies to: whole area

### [SOU-R07] Bassett Neighbourhood Plan policies BAS 8, BAS 9, BAS 10 and BAS 14
Detail: The plan calls for Bassett Green Village’s conservation-area character and green to be retained; policy BAS 9 resists development that damages protected trees or other trees of good amenity value. BAS 10 requires existing grass verges to be retained and construction-damaged verges reinstated in new development or redevelopment. BAS 14 requires drainage evidence for development of more than one dwelling. These are development-policy provisions, not a statement that routine lawn care requires a planning application.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf]  
Applies to: SOU-N04, SOU-N07, SOU-N08, SOU-N09, SOU-N10, SOU-N17

### [SOU-R08] Southampton City Council high-hedges procedure
Detail: The council defines a qualifying high hedge as two or more adjacent evergreen or semi-evergreen trees or shrubs taller than two metres. It accepts complaints about neighbouring private hedges under Part 8 of the Anti-social Behaviour Act 2003 after other means of resolving the dispute have been exhausted. Following assessment, it can take no further action or serve a Remedial Notice. This procedure concerns a particular type of boundary hedge; it is not a general maximum height for every garden hedge **(dated: September 2025)**.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/environment/trees-grass-hedges-and-leaves/reporting-issues-with-trees-or-vegetation/high-hedges-complaint/]  
Applies to: whole area

### [SOU-R09] Southern Water Hampshire and Isle of Wight Temporary Use Ban
Detail: The ban that began on 10 July 2026 restricts ordinary household hosepipe garden watering in the affected Southern Water supply area and was still reported in force in early October **(dated: October 2026)**.[https://www.itv.com/news/meridian/2026-07-10/hosepipe-ban-comes-into-force-as-third-heatwave-hits][https://www.preparedbritain.co.uk/trackers/hosepipe-bans] Southern Water publishes exemptions, including conditions concerning some recently planted trees and hedging, and requirements for qualifying drip systems; those exceptions are narrower than a general permission to hose-water new lawns.[https://www.southernwater.co.uk/help-and-support/hosepipe-ban-exemptions/] The restriction applies by water supply area, not by Southampton conservation-area boundary.  
Applies to: whole area

## 6. DEMAND BY AREA

**Drainage-led landscaping has its clearest documented fit on particular water-affected plots, not across whole postcode districts.** Garden drainage, Drainage solutions, Grading and resloping and appropriately drained Patio paving relate to the named tidal gardens in St Denys [SOU-N01] and Woodmill [SOU-N19], the Bitterne Manor frontage [SOU-N02], lower Millbrook [SOU-N06] and the Holly Brook or Monks Brook corridors [SOU-N04, SOU-N03].[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf] Shirley [SOU-N05], Townhill Park [SOU-N16] and parts of Freemantle [SOU-N18] add documented groundwater or surface-water considerations, but no source establishes uniform conditions across their gardens.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]

**Larger-plot design and maintenance belong most clearly to Bassett’s documented housing contrasts.** Garden design, Custom landscape design, Lawn landscaping, Groundskeeping and Tree planting fit the larger gardens of Bassett Heath [SOU-N07] and Ridgemount [SOU-N08] in a different way from Garden work, Lawn mowing and maintenance or Fencing installation on the denser Flowers Estate [SOU-N09] (inferred).[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf] Retaining walls, Outdoor step construction, Deck design and Patio design have a distinct physical rationale where the documented Bassett, Uplands or Old Woolston terrain changes level [SOU-N04, SOU-N13, SOU-N14].[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/sbsf433l/bassett-neighbourhood-plan-publication-version_af.pdf][http://www.ueha.co.uk/uploads/2/5/6/4/25647797/ueha__conservation_guidelines__aug_2020.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/yyncgowi/woolston_conservation_area_appraisal_january_2010_tcm63-363376.pdf]

**Conservation-area work has an additional boundary and tree dimension.** Paths, driveways, fences and tree services in Ethelburt Avenue [SOU-N10], Portswood Residents’ Gardens [SOU-N11] and Oakmount Triangle [SOU-N12] intersect with explicit controls on visible hardstanding, enclosures or protected trees.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/bhlodkjj/ethelburt-avenue-conservation-area-appraisal-management-plan-approved_af.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/4ian33xb/portswood_residents_garden_conservation_area_af.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ni3f52xv/otra-character-appraisal-management-plan_tcm63-363345.pdf] Across planted areas, Lawn care, Turf management, Mulching and Tree planting also sit alongside the reported Southern Water restrictions **(dated: October 2026)**.[https://www.southernwater.co.uk/help-and-support/hosepipe-ban-exemptions/][https://www.preparedbritain.co.uk/trackers/hosepipe-bans]

## 7. NEARBY CONTRAST

### Eastleigh
Eastleigh Borough’s flood assessment describes much of its centre as Bracklesham Beds, a sand-and-clay mixture, and identifies heavy, often poorly drained soils where London Clay outcrops. It treats the Itchen, Monks Brook and Hamble as principal river systems. Southampton instead has a distinctly extensive tidal urban frontage alongside its brook risks.[https://www.eastleigh.gov.uk/media/14372/sfra-part-8-eastleigh-bc-final-nov-23.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]  
Kind of difference: ground and flood setting

### Totton
Totton is outside Southampton City Council’s boundary, in New Forest District. The district flood assessment identifies Southampton Water flood-zone land at Totton and a modelled tidal effect near its station; it also identifies Bartley Water among significant surface-water corridors. Those are different named catchments from Southampton’s Holly Brook and lower urban Itchen locations.[https://www.newforest.gov.uk/media/4013/PfSH-SFRA-NFDC-Part-10-New-Forest-District-2024/pdf/PfSH_SFRA_NFDC_Part_10_New_Forest_District_2024.pdf?m=1719398826693][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]  
Kind of difference: authority and watercourses

### New Forest National Park
The National Park Authority, rather than Southampton City Council, manages planning and protected-tree matters inside the park. It describes development as managed to preserve the protected landscape and supplies its own tree-work and conservation-area procedures. Southampton’s garden constraints instead arise from its city planning designations, urban plots, brook corridors and tidal frontage.[https://www.newforestnpa.gov.uk/planning-home-page/][https://www.newforestnpa.gov.uk/planning-home-page/trees-and-planning/submitting-a-tree-work-application/][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]  
Kind of difference: planning authority and landscape designation

### Portsmouth
Portsmouth’s flood guidance identifies a predominantly island-based tidal exposure: approximately 47% of its land was mapped in Flood Zones 2 and 3 in the cited assessment, with extensive risk across Portsea Island. Southampton’s council guidance instead describes higher northern ground descending to two tidal rivers, with particular inland brook corridors. The two cities consequently have different distributions of low garden ground.[https://www.portsmouth.gov.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/Guidance-Portsmouth-City-Council.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/s1znees1/southampton-level-2-sfra-main-report-may-2017_tcm63-390513.pdf]  
Kind of difference: topography and flood distribution

## 8. GAPS

- Southampton’s official SuDS guidance says urban soils are **largely unsurveyed**. It does not verify soil type or acidity garden by garden, nor a reliable acidity map for the named neighbourhoods.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/ypaj1ord/suds-guidance_tcm63-397136.pdf]
- No sufficiently local official evidence established a Southampton neighbourhood-by-neighbourhood coastal salt-spray limit, prevailing-wind exposure, frost-pocket map, or deer and rabbit pressure.
- Southampton City Council confirms ash dieback at a small number of council sites but does not identify affected neighbourhoods on the page found; no neighbourhood-specific tree-disease claim was made.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/environment/trees-grass-hedges-and-leaves/reporting-issues-with-trees-or-vegetation/nuisance-trees/]
- The council records Japanese knotweed on council land and describes its effects on hard surfaces, but the located material did not identify verified affected Southampton residential neighbourhoods. It was therefore not assigned to an estate or private garden.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/gmybq5ua/service-commitments-green-2019_tcm63-404766.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/people-places/parks-open-spaces/parks/park-management/]
- Reliable garden dimensions, rear-access measurements and consistent housing-era profiles were unavailable for several wider neighbourhoods, including Shirley, Freemantle, Bitterne Manor and Swaythling. Profiles were limited to the streets or conditions official documents actually identify.
- The council-hosted Uplands Estate design-guidance PDF did not open; another copy was obtained from the **Uplands Estate Homeowners’ Association**, an estate representative rather than a trade competitor.[https://www.planning.data.gov.uk/entity/44004327][http://www.ueha.co.uk/uploads/2/5/6/4/25647797/ueha__conservation_guidelines__aug_2020.pdf]
- The Old Woolston appraisal *recommended consideration* of additional Article 4 directions. Evidence located did not establish that those proposed directions were subsequently made, so they were not presented as operative rules.[https://www.southampton.gov.uk/media/yyncgowi/woolston_conservation_area_appraisal_january_2010_tcm63-363376.pdf]
- Search results promoting Southampton paving and dropped-kerb businesses, as well as landscaping-related marketing pages, were excluded as competitor-type sources; no claim above depends on them.
- Hosepipe-ban search results also surfaced Southern Water pages announcing the end of the **earlier** Hampshire ban. Those pages were not treated as evidence that the separate July **2026** restriction had ended; early-October reporting continued to list the 2026 restriction **(dated: October 2026)**.[https://www.southernwater.co.uk/latest-news/end-of-hosepipe-ban-for-hampshire-and-isle-of-wight/][https://www.itv.com/news/meridian/2026-07-10/hosepipe-ban-comes-into-force-as-third-heatwave-hits][https://www.preparedbritain.co.uk/trackers/hosepipe-bans]
- No estate-agent or property-listing source was used. The homeowners’ association copy used for Uplands is a **weak source for current legal status**, so statutory-control claims elsewhere rely on council material where available.[http://www.ueha.co.uk/uploads/2/5/6/4/25647797/ueha__conservation_guidelines__aug_2020.pdf][https://www.southampton.gov.uk/environment/trees-grass-hedges-and-leaves/protected/tpo-map/]

END OF DOSSIER
